findings.evidence: `CauchyPrincipalValue.lean` exposes the pointwise value API at lines 109, 154, 159, and 165; `rg` in `CauchyPrincipalValueOn.lean` finds only `HasCauchyPV`, `hasCauchyPV_iff`, `.intro`, `CauchyPVExists`, bridges, and zero/const/congr lemmas at lines 86, 97, 110, 121, 138, 156, 175, 184, and 204, with no set-level value or uniqueness declaration.
findings.fix: Add the set-level value and uniqueness API now, or keep the prescribed-witness machinery internal until the public `HasCauchyPV` interface is characterized by those lemmas.
findings.issue: `HasCauchyPV` is a public existence-and-value predicate over an existential excision set, but the set-level API has no canonical `cauchyPV`, `HasCauchyPV.cauchyPV_eq`, `HasCauchyPV.unique`, or `CauchyPVExists.hasCauchyPV_cauchyPV` analogue; consumers cannot turn `CauchyPVExists` into a predicate at a named value or prove two value witnesses agree through the public interface.

summary: The new set-level PV predicate exposes an existence-and-value public interface but does not provide the value/uniqueness API needed to make that interface usable without unfolding or redoing limit uniqueness across witnesses.
